newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's YPF gets ok for share float.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's YPF gets ok for share float.

text.p: Argentine oil company YPF SA said Wednesday it had got the approval of over 90 percent of employees for plans to float their 10 percent of the company's share capital.

The company said in a letter to the Buenos Aires stock exchange that it had not yet got the approval of the Argentine government for the share float, which it announced last week, but would be starting formalities to get it soon.
The brief statement from the company gave no further details.

The privatized oil giant said one week ago that the plans to float the 35.5 million C class shares in the hands of staff required the prior approval of 90 percent of employees and of the Argentine government.
Shares in the company are currently at all time highs, closing in Buenos Aires Wednesday at $30.7.

After the company was privatized by the Peronist government in 1993, 70 percent of the stock was listed in local and international markets, 20 percent retained by the government and 10 percent assigned for purchase by employees.
